code-reranker-finetuning

Code Reranker Fine-tuning

Fine-tune a fixed BGE reranker to improve top-five code retrieval over shared BM25 and local embedding candidates.

Domain
code retrieval
Primary focus
Fixed-backbone cross-encoder fine-tuning
Primary metric
Accuracy@5 gain normalized by candidate headroom
reranker trainingsearch-swe
On this page
OverviewRuntime and requirementsPublic input and output contractInputsOutputsEvaluation

Runtime and requirements

  • Agent budget: 6 hours
  • Compute: 8 CPUs, 32 GiB RAM, 100 GiB storage; one GPU
  • Network: disabled in both task phases; no task API keys
  • Verifier budget: 10,800 seconds
  • Phase limits: 2,700 seconds for first-stage retrieval; 7,200 seconds for both rerankers

Only the weights of BAAI/bge-reranker-base may change. Preserve its architecture, parameter names and shapes, configuration and tokenizer. Do not modify the frozen embedding model or candidate policy, blend first-stage scores into logits, or use outside training queries, labels, models or services.

Public input and output contract

Inputs

  • /task/data/corpus.jsonl — 8,765 code documents with _id, title and text.
  • /task/data/train.jsonl — 5,000 queries, each with one positive and an empty negative array.
  • /task/models/bge-reranker-base — the supplied reranker backbone.
  • /task/models/bge-base-en-v1.5 — the frozen local embedding model for candidate mining.
  • /app/starter/train.sh and /app/starter/train.py — editable training and export starter.

There is no public validation split; a local training holdout is allowed. Evaluation uses 200 questions withheld from the agent.

Outputs

Save a complete checkpoint under /app/output/model, including config.json, model.safetensors and the original tokenizer files. Only this directory transfers; submitted training scripts are not executed.

The verifier loads weights offline with remote code disabled and safetensors required. Both rerankers use the tokenizer from the trusted backbone; the four required submitted tokenizer files must still match byte for byte. Additional submitted tokenizer metadata cannot change inference.

Evaluation

The fixed first stage combines BM25 Top-200 and local BGE Top-200 using equal-weight reciprocal rank fusion with k=60. Keep the entire deduplicated union of 200–400 candidates. Both rerankers score the same full question/document pairs with joint 512-token truncation and batch size 16; equal logits preserve RRF order. The full contract fixes tokenization, pooling and branch tie-breaking.

Accuracy@5 is one when any relevant document appears among the first five reranked candidates. Let B be baseline mean Accuracy@5, S the submitted mean, and C the fraction of questions with a relevant document anywhere in the fixed candidate union:

reward = clamp((S - B) / (C - B), 0, 1), when C > B
reward = 0, otherwise

All 200 questions remain in every denominator, including first-stage misses. B and C are recomputed in each evaluation, not taken from historical trials. Invalid checkpoints, loading failures or phase timeouts yield zero. Scoring and checkpoint checks are deterministic; there is no trajectory judge.

The full contract is in the benchmark's task instructions, task documentation, and runtime configuration.
